GraphService（C++）

Service introduction

GraphService is the main graph management service of Atom SDK and is responsible for the complete life cycle of the graph: creation, query, copy, delete, import and export, and putting the entire graph into operation. All operations are performed on the "main graph" hosted on the server side, which is different from the subgraphs managed by GraphNodeService.

Header file:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
// or quoted individually(Pass client.hpp automatically included)
#include "atom_sdk/services/graph.hpp"

Entrance:

atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
atom::sdk::GraphService& gs = client.graph();

Applicable scenarios

  • Initialize worksheet on program startup (create or import)

  • Dynamically manage multi-image workflow (copy, delete)

  • Export and archive configured graphs or migrate them to other servers

  • Control the operation and cleaning of the entire image

Recommended calling order

create_graph / load_graph
        ↓
  open_graph          ← Enter editing mode,cooperate NodeService Edit node
        ↓
  run_graph           ← Execute the whole picture(Automatically manage timestamps internally)
        ↓
  clear_graph         ← Clean up the running state(Optional)
        ↓
 release_graph        ← Release editing resources(Optional)
        ↓
 delete_graph         ← Destroy chart(Optional)

Interface detailed explanation

create_graph

JsonObject create_graph(const CreateGraphParams& params) const;

Purpose: Create a new blank image on the server side.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

The unique name of the picture. It cannot have the same name as an existing picture.

params.description

std::optional<std::string>

Optional picture description information, passing std::nullopt means no description

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains meta information of the newly created graph, key fields:

field type Description

name

string

Picture name

id

string/int

Figure unique ID

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Create a graph without description
    auto result = client.graph().create_graph({"my_detection_graph"});

    // Create a diagram with description
    auto result2 = client.graph().create_graph(
        {"my_seg_graph", "Main image for instance segmentation"});

    std::string name = result.at("name").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "Create diagram:" << name << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

list_graphs

JsonArray list_graphs() const;

Purpose: List all currently visible images on the server.

Parameters: None

*Return value: * JsonArray, each element in the array is JsonValue (internally an object), containing the basic information of the graph:

field type Description

name

string

Picture name

description

string

Picture description (may be empty)

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    atom::sdk::JsonArray graphs = client.graph().list_graphs();

    std::cout << "share " << graphs.size() << " Picture:" << std::endl;
    for (const auto& g : graphs) {
        const auto& obj = g;
        std::string name = obj.at("name").get<std::string>();
        std::cout << "  - " << name << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail

JsonArray get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail() const;

Purpose: Read the summary list of all custom sub-images, excluding thumbnails, suitable for template selection lists.

auto custom_subgraphs = client.graph().get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail();

copy_graph

JsonObject copy_graph(const CopyGraphParams& params) const;

Use: Copy an existing picture and create a copy with a new name.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Source image name (must already exist)

params.new_graph_name

std::string

New picture name (cannot have the same name as an existing picture)

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains meta information of the new graph, the structure is the same as create_graph return value.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    auto result = client.graph().copy_graph(
        {"production_graph", "test_graph_copy"});

    std::string new_name = result.at("name").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "Copy completed,New picture title:" << new_name << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

edit_graph_name

JsonValue edit_graph_name(const EditGraphNameParams& params) const;

Purpose: Modify the picture name. The server currently usually returns true.

client.graph().edit_graph_name({"demo_graph", "demo_graph_v2"});

edit_graph_comment

JsonValue edit_graph_comment(const EditGraphCommentParams& params) const;

Purpose: Modify drawing notes. SDK will automatically bring the currently cached timestamp.

client.graph().edit_graph_comment({"demo_graph", "New process notes"});

delete_graph

JsonValue delete_graph(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Delete the specified graph and clear the local timestamp cache simultaneously.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

The name of the image to be deleted

*Return value: * JsonValue, usually operation status information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    auto result = client.graph().delete_graph("obsolete_graph");
    std::cout << "Delete successfully" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

get_all_nodes_info

JsonObject get_all_nodes_info() const;

Purpose: Read all node definitions currently registered on the server to understand the available node types.

Parameters: None

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains all node definitions. Usually the node type name is key and the node description is value.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    auto nodes_info = client.graph().get_all_nodes_info();

    std::cout << "Number of registered nodes:" << nodes_info.size() << std::endl;
    for (const auto& [key, val] : nodes_info) {
        std::cout << "  Node type:" << key << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info

JsonObject get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Read the model information that the deep learning node in the graph depends on.

auto dl_models = client.graph().get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info("demo_graph");

get_graph_custom_nodes

JsonObject get_graph_custom_nodes(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Read the custom node information referenced in the graph.

auto custom_nodes = client.graph().get_graph_custom_nodes("demo_graph");

get_graph_workcell_models_info

JsonObject get_graph_workcell_models_info(
    const std::string& graph_name,
    std::optional<std::string> graph_node_id = std::nullopt) const;

Purpose: Read the main image or specify the workcell model information corresponding to graph node.

auto workcell = client.graph().get_graph_workcell_models_info(
    "demo_graph",
    "graph-node-id");

get_graph_bindings

JsonObject get_graph_bindings(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Read the binding information exposed to the outside world by the specified graph, including the meta description of input binding and output binding.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

*Return value: * JsonObject, including binding name, type, data format and other description information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    auto bindings = client.graph().get_graph_bindings("detection_graph");

    for (const auto& [key, val] : bindings) {
        std::cout << "binding:" << key << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_graph_json_data

JsonObject get_graph_json_data(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Read the original JSON structure of the graph. status will be added to the returned object.

auto graph_json = client.graph().get_graph_json_data("demo_graph");
std::cout << graph_json.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

load_graph

JsonObject load_graph(const LoadGraphParams& params) const;

Purpose: Import (load) the graph from a local file to the server, and the server will register the graph under the name graph_name. Before importing, SDK will first read the current graph list; if params.graph_name already exists, AtomError will be thrown, /Graph/LoadGraph will not be called, and the existing graph will not be overwritten. You need to use a new graph name or delete the existing graph and try again.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

The name of the graph used on the server after importing

params.file_path

std::filesystem::path

local map file path (usually .json or SDK proprietary format)

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing import result information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    std::filesystem::path graph_file = "/data/graphs/detection_v2.json";
    auto result = client.graph().load_graph({"detection_v2", graph_file});

    std::cout << "Picture import successful" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

import_extension_nodes_by_path

JsonValue import_extension_nodes_by_path(const JsonObject& extension_nodes) const;

Purpose: Import the extended node file decompressed by load_graph. This interface is usually Called after load_graph, the parameters are passed to load_graph and extensionNodes in the return value field, do not pass the entire load_graph return object.

parameters type Description

extension_nodes

JsonObject

load_graph The extensionNodes field in the return value

Example:

auto loaded = client.graph().load_graph({"detection_v2", graph_file});
const auto* extension_nodes = atom::sdk::json::if_contains(loaded, "extensionNodes");
if (extension_nodes != nullptr && extension_nodes->is_object() &&
    !extension_nodes->empty()) {
    auto imported = client.graph().import_extension_nodes_by_path(
        *extension_nodes);
    std::cout << atom::sdk::json::serialize(imported) << std::endl;
}

export_graph

JsonObject export_graph(const ExportGraphParams& params) const;

Purpose: Export the server graph and its accompanying model information and custom node information into an archiveable format.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

The name of the graph to be exported

params.dl_models_info

JsonObject

Deep learning model description information attached (can be empty)

params.custom_nodes

JsonObject Custom node description attached to

(can be empty)

*Return value: * JsonObject, including exported graph data and meta information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Export graph structure only,Comes with no additional information
    auto exported = client.graph().export_graph({"detection_v2"});

    // Comes with model information export
    atom::sdk::JsonObject models_info;
    // models_info["yolo_v8"] = atom::sdk::JsonObject{...};
    auto exported2 = client.graph().export_graph({"detection_v2", models_info});

    std::cout << "Figure exported successfully" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

open_graph

JsonObject open_graph(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Open the graph and enter the editing state. You can then edit the nodes in the graph through NodeService.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing the current status information of the graph.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Open the image and enter editing mode
    auto result = client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // can be used later NodeService add/Edit node
    auto& ns = client.node();
    auto node = ns.create_node({"my_graph", "DetectionNode"});

    std::cout << "Image is open,Can start editing" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

release_graph

JsonValue release_graph(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Release the editing state resources of the graph and make the graph exit the editing mode (without deleting the graph).

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

*Return value: * JsonValue, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // ... Edit diagram ...

    // Editing completed,Release editing resources
    client.graph().release_graph("my_graph");

    return 0;
}

run_graph

JsonObject run_graph(
    const std::string& graph_name,
    std::optional<double> timeout_seconds = 30.0) const;

Purpose: Run the entire main graph and trigger all nodes in the graph to execute in topological order. SDK will poll the server for responses until finish is true or exceeds timeout_seconds.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

timeout_seconds

std::optional<double>

Polling waiting timeout, default is 30.0 seconds; passing std::nullopt means waiting until completion or the server reports an error

*Return value: * JsonObject, including running results and status information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Run the main image,most wait 60 seconds
    auto result = client.graph().run_graph("detection_graph", 60.0);

    // Check if the run is complete
    if (result.contains("finish")) {
        bool finished = result.at("finish").get<bool>();
        std::cout << "Run completed:" << (finished ? "Yes" : "No") << std::endl;
    }
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

clear_graph

JsonObject clear_graph(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Clean up the running intermediate state of the graph, usually called before re-running to ensure that the state is clean.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Clean and rerun
    client.graph().clear_graph("detection_graph");
    auto result = client.graph().run_graph("detection_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

get_timestamp

JsonObject get_timestamp(const std::string& graph_name) const;

Purpose: Read the current timestamp of the graph to confirm the data version and synchronization status.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Picture name

*Return value: * JsonObject, including timestamp information:

field type Description

timestamp

int64/double

Figure current timestamp

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    auto ts_info = client.graph().get_timestamp("detection_graph");

    if (ts_info.contains("timestamp")) {
        double ts = ts_info.at("timestamp").get<double>();
        std::cout << "current timestamp:" << ts << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

Complete example

The following shows a complete diagram management process: creating diagrams, opening for editing, running, cleaning, and deleting.

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>
#include <stdexcept>

int main() {
    try {
        atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
        auto& gs = client.graph();

        // 1. List existing diagrams
        auto graphs = gs.list_graphs();
        std::cout << "Number of existing pictures:" << graphs.size() << std::endl;

        // 2. Import diagram from file
        gs.load_graph({"demo_graph", "/data/demo_graph.json"});
        std::cout << "Picture import completed" << std::endl;

        // 3. open diagram(Enter editing mode)
        gs.open_graph("demo_graph");

        // 4. View available node types
        auto node_types = gs.get_all_nodes_info();
        std::cout << "Number of available node types:" << node_types.size() << std::endl;

        // 5. Run the entire graph
        auto run_result = gs.run_graph("demo_graph");
        std::cout << "Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

        // 6. Read timestamp,Confirm result timeliness
        auto ts = gs.get_timestamp("demo_graph");
        if (ts.contains("timestamp")) {
            std::cout << "Figure timestamp:" << ts.at("timestamp").get<double>() << std::endl;
        }

        // 7. Clean up the running state
        gs.clear_graph("demo_graph");

        // 8. Release editing resources
        gs.release_graph("demo_graph");

        // 9. Delete picture(Optional)
        gs.delete_graph("demo_graph");
        std::cout << "Demonstration completed" << std::endl;

    } catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
        std::cerr << "SDK Error:" << e.what() << std::endl;
        return 1;
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::cerr << "Abnormal:" << e.what() << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    return 0;
}
